title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page. Grothendieck takes C to be the category of supersingular elliptic curves in characteristic p, with Hom tensored to remove p-torsion (the 'Hom mod ...' line). By Deuring, C is a 'Deuring category' attached to the definite quaternion algebra D over Q ramified exactly at p and ∞, i.e. the element of order 2 in Br(Q) with invariants at {p, ∞}. From this datum he builds a gerbe G over Spec Z[1/p]. Its lien is described (with hesitations) via G_m together with an invertible rank-2 representation; as transcribed the lien symbol reads both as H_ℓ and \hat G. It is an integral (prime-to-p) Tannakian gerbe of 'supersingular motives'. Over A' = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ he compares it with the gerbe H_{A'} built from the prime-to-p Tate module data A'(1) = ∏ Z_ℓ(1). A fibre functor over A' (a trivialisation) comes together with an isomorphism φ(T) ≃ A'(1), where T is the determinant / Tate object.

This page.
(1) There is an equivalence G_{A'} ≃ H_{A'}, i.e. the ℓ-adic (prime-to-p) realisation identifies the base-changed motivic gerbe with the 'étale' gerbe.
(2) The question is how much of C is captured by this. Given C, its position inside G_{A'}, up to isomorphism, is an invariant in a torsor Π under H^1(A', μ_2) = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ^*/Z_ℓ^{*2}. Each factor is Z/2 for ℓ odd and (Z/2)^2 for ℓ = 2, computed with fppf cohomology since μ_2 is not étale over Z_2. So the integral ℓ-adic structure is pinned down only up to a 'square-class' (determinant/spinor-type) twist at each ℓ.
(3) The gerbe G_{A'} is itself determined only up to non-unique equivalence. Its automorphisms coming from global μ_2-torsors act through H^1(Z[1/p], μ_2). By Kummer theory, with Pic(Z[1/p]) = 0, this group is Z[1/p]^*/Z[1/p]^{*2} = ⟨-1, p⟩ ≅ (Z/2)^2. The two generators correspond to the quadratic extensions by √-1 and √p.
(4) The well-defined invariant therefore lives in Π/ρ(Z/2×Z/2). Here ρ: H^1(Z[1/p], μ_2) → H^1(A', μ_2) is localisation, sending -1 and p to their square classes in each Z_ℓ^*. For odd ℓ, a class is trivial iff it is a square mod ℓ; for ℓ = 2 one tests mod 8, as the margin notes.
(5) Margins.
- There is no natural origin in ∏ Z_ℓ^*/squares, so Π is a genuine torsor, not a group.
- The ambiguity (Z/2)^2 can be killed by extra structure: (a) a polarisation at ∞, which fixes the sign class -1; (b) an 'orientation' at p, which fixes the class of p.

Purpose: to classify integral (Z[1/p]) forms of the motivic Galois gerbe of supersingular elliptic curves. He measures the gap between the motivic and étale integral structures by a Galois-cohomological square-class invariant, modulo global units. This is an adelic 'genus versus class' analysis in Tannakian language.
errors: Labelling slip: Grothendieck says (1,0) corresponds to √-1 and (0,1) to √p, but then defines ρ(1,0)_ℓ by whether p is a square (adding 'resp. -1' as a correction). The roles of the two generators are swapped or inconsistently annotated.
The criterion 'p square in Z_ℓ^* ⇔ p square in (Z/ℓ)^*' is only valid for ℓ odd. For ℓ = 2 one needs mod 8; Grothendieck corrects this in the margin.
H^1(Z_2, μ_2) ≅ (Z/2)^2 requires flat (fppf) cohomology, since μ_2 is not étale over Z_2. This is implicit, not stated.
The ℓ-adic components should exclude only ℓ = p; '∞' in the product index is notation, not a prime.

ideas.what: Supersingular elliptic curves in char p form a category governed by the definite quaternion algebra ramified at {p, ∞} (Deuring), viewed as a Tannakian gerbe
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence; motivic Galois gerbe of supersingular motives / Langlands–Rapoport pseudomotivic groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941); Tannakian version Grothendieck/Saavedra, Milne, Langlands–Rapoport (1987)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra Rivano's thesis (1972) and Deligne–Milne; not by Grothendieck himself

ideas.what: Integral (over Z[1/p]) gerbe compared with its prime-to-p adelic realisation, via an equivalence G_{A'} ≃ H_{A'}
ideas.modern_name: Integral Tannakian gerbes; integral ℓ-adic / adelic realisation of motives over finite fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Largely undeveloped; related to Kisin's integral Langlands–Rapoport work and Milne's motives over finite fields

ideas.what: Invariant in a torsor under ∏ Z_ℓ^*/Z_ℓ^{*2}, taken modulo the image of H^1(Z[1/p], μ_2) = ⟨-1, p⟩
ideas.modern_name: Local-global square-class / spinor-norm type obstruction; adelic class set modulo global units
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Eichler, spinor genus theory) in lattice language

ideas.what: Killing the ambiguity by extra structure: polarisation at ∞ and 'orientation' at p
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of Tannakian data by polarisation (Weil-type positivity) and p-adic orientation

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a classification of integral (Z[1/p]) forms of the motivic Galois gerbe of supersingular elliptic curves. The residual invariant is a square-class element of ∏_ℓ Z_ℓ^*/Z_ℓ^{*2} modulo ⟨-1, p⟩, removable by polarisation at ∞ plus an orientation at p. Integral motivic gerbes over Z[1/p] with explicit cohomological invariants of this sort are not a standard topic in the literature.
missed.quote: on trouve un invariant dans un quotient Π/ρ(Z/2Z), où Π est le torseur sous H^1(A',μ_2) = ∏ Z_ℓ^*/Z_ℓ^{*2} des trivialisations de H_{A'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral structures on the Langlands–Rapoport / motivic gerbe over finite fields are of current interest (Kisin, Kisin–Madapusi–Shin). An explicit μ_2-cohomological description of the ambiguity, and the role of an 'orientation at p', is a concrete toy model.

missed.claim: Implicit link between Tannakian gerbe classification and genus/spinor-genus theory of quaternion orders: square classes modulo global units, i.e. a determinant/norm obstruction.
missed.quote: NB il n'y a absolument pas de façon naturelle de choisir une origine dans Z_ℓ^* mod ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Reformulates Eichler-style class-set computations as torsor or gerbe invariants. It is modest but suggestive for integral motivic Galois theory.

deep.surprise_reason: A detailed integral treatment of the supersingular motivic gerbe over Z[1/p] in 1965-ish notes predates Langlands–Rapoport. The actual cohomological computation is routine Kummer theory, and the thread is clearly exploratory.
transcription_corrections: 'C dans G_{A^*}' should probably read 'C dans G_{A'}' (A' with a prime). The superscript note is 'de G_{A'} ... ici fixée/finie'.
'représentant un point' is crossed out and replaced by 'à iso. près'.
The 2-power-line likely reads 'déterminée seulement à équivalence (non unique) près'.
In the margin, 'Z_ℓ^* mod (Z/ℓZ)^{*2}' is likely 'Z_ℓ^* mod Z_ℓ^{*2}', i.e. via (Z/ℓZ)^* for ℓ≠2 and via (Z/8Z)^* for ℓ=2.
'ℓ ≠ p, ∞' under the product is as written. 'Z/2Z' in ρ's source should be 'Z/2Z × Z/2Z', as inserted.
